_comment: Authoritative project facts: hand-edited, enforced by scripts/check_structure.py (check_H, CONVENTIONS section 15). Choose one frontend stack; list shipped stacks/transports under 'available'.
name: project_keel

template._comment: Keel is a copier template: files suffixed .jinja are rendered, everything else is copied verbatim. `twins` declares every .jinja and what it is FOR, so a new one cannot appear unnoticed — scripts/check_structure.py check_N enforces it, render-free, so it runs in the 3.6 pre-commit gate. 'parity' = must reproduce keel's own file except where templated; 'divergence' = must NOT (the difference is the point); 'generated' = copier writes it into a new project and keel commits none of its own. A generated project has no .jinja files, so check_N is silent there.

structure._comment: Top-level directories this project adds beyond the CONVENTIONS section 2 taxonomy, by name. scripts/check_structure.py check_B errors on any other non-hidden top-level directory, on a name here that does not exist or is already in the taxonomy, and on a declared directory without README.md and CLAUDE.md. Names only: the directory's own README.md summary says why it exists.

rosters._comment: The README.md files that are rosters, by repo-relative path. scripts/check_structure.py check_S holds each to its directory through its '## What ships here' table, and errors on a listed README without that table, on a listed path with no file, and on a README carrying the heading that readmes does not list. The list lives here, in a file agents.protected_paths refuses an agent edit to, so a README edit cannot turn its own roster check off; an absent block lists nothing, so every roster README errors.

adr._comment: The two ADR number spaces (docs/adr/keel/K-0013-template-and-project-adr-number-spaces.md, CONVENTIONS section 19). project_dir holds this project's own ADRs, NNNN-<slug>.md numbered from 0001; template_dir holds the ADRs the template ships, template_prefix + NNNN-<slug>.md, shown as ADR-K-NNNN; number_digits is N. Each space numbers on its own. template_adrs names every file the template ships in template_dir: it is the template's to write, and a project does not add to it, because a project's decision under a free K- number would meet the template's next ADR of that number on update. scripts/check_structure.py check_Y holds every ADR file to the space it sits in, a template-space file to template_adrs and template_adrs to the files, every kind: adr document to one of the two directories, its title to its file name, and a number to one file per space; a missing or malformed block is an error once the tree has a `kind: adr` document.

agents._comment: What an edit an agent proposes may never reach: the code, configuration and approved text that judge it. scripts/apply_refactor.py plan_edits reads this block through scripts/config_loader.py and refuses, before any write and so in a dry run too, an edit to a covered path, naming the edit, the path and the key that protects it with its reason. protected_paths maps a repo-relative path to its reason and covers that path and everything under it; protected_names maps a file name, or a glob over one such as `*.test.*`, to its reason and covers each name it matches in any directory; editable_names maps a file name or glob to its reason and carves the names it matches back out of a protected directory. Precedence: a protected name refuses, else an editable name allows, else a protected path refuses. Matching compares case-folded path parts, so a case variant is refused too, and an edit is judged twice, on the path as written and on its realpath, so a symlink cannot launder a judge file; an absolute path, a `..` part and a file with more than one hard link are refused outright. Below this list sits a second rule no entry lifts: a file git does not track is refused, so git's own state, an ignored file and the toolchain the gate runs (.venv, node_modules) stay out of reach even where no entry names them. protected_paths and protected_names must each hold at least one entry, every reason must be non-blank, and protected_paths must cover config/project.json itself, or the policy is a config fault; editable_names may be empty, the setting with no carve-out. The map only refuses: no flag lifts it, and only a human edit of this file removes an entry. An entry for a path this tree lacks protects nothing and is not an error. It does not reach an interactive agent's direct edit outside scripts/apply_refactor.py, which needs hooks or permission rules, not built. docs/adr/keel/K-0026-agent-edits-cannot-reach-the-judge.md is the decision.

protected_paths..claude: the hooks and skills that launch the agents and run the gates on Stop
protected_paths..copier-answers.yml: the commit copier update merges from; absent in the template
protected_paths..copier-answers.yml.jinja: the twin .copier-answers.yml renders from; absent in a generated project
protected_paths..git: git's own state: .git/config can set core.fsmonitor, which runs inside the gate's own git status, .git/hooks run on commit, and in a linked worktree .git is the file naming the repository
protected_paths..github: the CI workflows that run make verify and gate a release
protected_paths..gitignore.jinja: the twin .gitignore renders from; absent in a generated project
protected_paths.CONVENTIONS.md: the taxonomy check_structure enforces; approved text (R-AGT-33)
protected_paths.agents: the brains, prompts and tool cards: an agent may not rewrite its own instructions or orchestration
protected_paths.api/rest_fastapi/export_openapi.py: make check-openapi's checker, a gate make check-all runs from outside scripts/
protected_paths.config: the judge's own configuration: project.json, this list included, and practices.json
protected_paths.copier.yml: the template's migrations and excludes; absent in a generated project
protected_paths.docs/adr: the decisions the gates enforce; accepted ADRs are immutable
protected_paths.docs/specs: the requirements make trace holds tests to
protected_paths.models: the adapters and the allowed_hosts boundary
protected_paths.pyproject.toml: ruff, mypy and pytest settings the lint, typecheck and test gates read
protected_paths.runtimes: the effect guard that bounds every agent step
protected_paths.scripts: check_structure and the other gate scripts, run_make_target, and apply_refactor itself
protected_paths.tests: the suite make test runs, conftest and the isolation guard included

protected_names.*.spec.*: a browser journey make test-fe-e2e runs (each app's e2e/*.spec.ts)
protected_names.*.test.*: a unit test make test-fe-unit runs (each app's src/**/*.test.ts and .test.tsx)
protected_names..gitattributes: the attributes git status reads (filters, line endings), so they decide what the tree-changed check sees
protected_names..gitignore: what git status leaves out in its directory, so what the tree-changed check and the gate evidence see
protected_names.AGENT.md: agent rules in every directory; approved text
protected_names.GNUmakefile: make verify's own recipes; make reads all three names
protected_names.Makefile: make verify's own recipes; make reads all three names
protected_names.conftest.py: pytest loads a conftest.py above tests/ too, so one anywhere on the path changes what make test runs
protected_names.eslint.config.js: the frontend lint and test gates' settings, make test-fe
protected_names.makefile: make verify's own recipes; make reads all three names
protected_names.package-lock.json: pins the frontend gates' own toolchain (vitest, playwright, tsc, eslint) make fe-install installs
protected_names.package.json: the frontend lint and test gates' settings, make test-fe
protected_names.playwright.config.ts: the frontend lint and test gates' settings, make test-fe
protected_names.tsconfig*.json: the TypeScript settings make typecheck-fe reads; tsconfig.app.json and tsconfig.node.json hold the strict flags
protected_names.vitest.config.ts: the frontend lint and test gates' settings, make test-fe

editable_names.README.md: every roster row doc_reviewer fixes lives in a README.md (115 of 115 measured); the one switch a gate reads in a README, its `## What ships here` heading, is held by rosters.readmes in this protected file, so a README edit cannot turn check_S off

doc_drift._comment: What a shipped document may not say (docs/guides/doc-style.md, CONVENTIONS section 15). A shipped document is any Markdown file, or its .md.jinja twin, whose path starts with none of history_paths; history_paths are the prefixes whose Markdown is history (a changelog, decisions, plans) and may name a campaign, a slice or a moment. forbidden_phrases maps a regular expression to the reason it is refused: a phrase true of one machine or one person, never a literal host, port or path. tests/integration/test_doc_drift.py reads both: in a shipped document's prose (code spans and fences are illustrations) it refuses a concrete work id in the work_naming grammar, any forbidden phrase, a loopback port that no non-Markdown file declares, and a citation of a document copier.yml never ships. The other keys name the documents a newcomer reads and what each must say, and the same test holds them: one_hop maps an entry document to the documents it links to directly; layout_heading is the README section whose tree lists every top-level directory that ships; roster is the guide index, whose rows each name their audiences from audiences, in that order; limits_guide names every waiver the checkers, the child-process allowlist, the isolation guard and this test grant, and holds the exit-code table scripts/exit_code_table.py generates from scripts/exit_codes.py and from every script make gate_target runs (make check-exit-codes fails a stale one); upgrade_guide gives every copier task and migration its own row in copier's order, names every exclusion and states the copier version floor (template only). settings_reference is the settings reference: tests/integration/test_reference_drift.py holds its rows derived-equal to every key of the JSON files it names, every copier question, make variable, environment variable and command-line flag, with each literal default. features_reference is the feature catalogue: the same test holds its rows to every feature the tree declares (each check letter, annotated make target with its effect label, checker script, copier job, gate test, scripts module another module outside tests/ imports, agent, MCP server, model and runtime adapter, workflow and agent skill) and requires each row to state its limits. A missing or malformed block fails that test.

forbidden_phrases.(?i)\\bon this host\\b: a claim about one machine; name the condition instead
forbidden_phrases.(?i)\\bthis host's\\b: a claim about one machine; name the condition instead
forbidden_phrases.(?:^|[\\s(`'\"])/home/[^/\\s]+/: a personal home-directory path; name the directory's role instead

work_naming._comment: How a campaign and a slice are named (CONVENTIONS section 20). campaign_id and slice_id are the id templates: <n> is the campaign number and <m> the slice number, each a positive integer with no leading zero, and slice_id is campaign_id plus a literal separator. A plan doc is a Markdown document whose frontmatter kind is in plan_kinds and that holds a table whose first header cell is slice_column. A cross-repository reference prefixes an id with the other project's `name` and a colon. A delivering commit carries one slice_trailer trailer with a bare slice id and may carry a backlog_trailer trailer whose value matches the backlog_id pattern. adoption_boundary is a commit before which trailers are not judged (null: every commit). scripts/check_structure.py check_Z holds the plan docs' Slice cells, campaign headings, slice order and prose mentions to this block; tests/integration/test_work_trailers.py holds commit trailers to it; a missing block is an error once the tree has a plan doc, and a malformed one always is.

make_targets._comment: Every annotated make target opens its `## ` help with an effect label from the closed vocabulary [local] [tree] [read] [cost] [write] (docs/adr/keel/K-0011-make-target-effect-labels.md). scripts/check_structure.py check_W validates this block and the labels; scripts/run_make_target.py runs only a target whose label falls inside gate_effects, sets gate_runner_var=1 last so WRITE_GUARD refuses a [write] target, accepts only the gate_vars as NAME=VALUE variables (each value one path-like word), and fails a run that changed what git sees. unattended_vars are the variables WRITE_GUARD refuses under; write_shapes are target-name suffixes that must be [write]; write_shape_exempt maps a write-shaped target that is not a write to the reason it keeps its label, and an entry naming a target no makefile defines, no write shape matches, no label annotates or that is already [write] is stale (docs/adr/keel/K-0015-write-shape-exemptions-and-guarded-recipe-converse.md); area_dir is the directory of <area>.mk makefiles (null: areas off); effect_proof_skip keeps a [local] target out of tests/integration/test_make_target_effects.py, by name and reason only; effect_proof_kept_dirs names the environment variables (keel ships the XDG base dirs) that sweep keeps while it runs each target under a fresh empty HOME, valued with the directory's relative path strictly inside HOME, used when the caller leaves the variable unset; the sweep fails a target that writes that HOME and does not see writes under the kept dirs; empty_test_selections names a pytest marker a `-m <marker>` recipe may run zero tests of, with the reason as the value (tests/selection_guard.py fails any other run of zero tests, and a run of that marker that ran a test makes the entry stale). gate_timeout_seconds is how long scripts/run_make_target.py lets one make run before it ends every process that make started (SIGTERM to the group, then SIGKILL after gate_stop_grace_seconds); both are optional, defaulted in scripts/config_loader.py KEYS, and --timeout overrides the first.

effect_proof_skip.new: generates a project outside the tree and needs DEST and a clean checkout
effect_proof_skip.audit-project: audits another project's tree and needs DEST; the template checkout proves it read-only in tests/integration/test_copier_audit.py, a whole-tree hash of DEST with .git included (in a generated project the target is a stub naming the template)
effect_proof_skip.run-api: a dev server that never exits
effect_proof_skip.run-web: a dev server that never exits and needs npm
effect_proof_skip.test: runs the whole suite, which holds this sweep, so it would run itself; tests/integration/test_write_guard.py runs its make-driving cases through the gate runner
effect_proof_skip.integration: runs the integration suite, which holds this proof
effect_proof_skip.long-scripts: judges recorded runs, and .launch/durations.json is git-ignored so a fresh clone has none, which is red by design (a pass over zero runs fails); tests/integration/test_launcher.py proves it read-only with a whole-tree digest
effect_proof_skip.secret-scan: runs the scanner `make secrets-install` records, and secrets.scanner.record_file is git-ignored so a fresh clone has none, which is red by design (exit 11, never a skip); tests/integration/test_secret_scan.py proves the history scan leaves what git lists unchanged
effect_proof_skip.test-fe: with a frontend app present, a hermetic clone has no node_modules, which is red by design (a suite over zero apps' tests fails); tests/integration/test_gate_scope.py drives it
effect_proof_skip.test-fe-unit: with a frontend app present, a hermetic clone has no node_modules, which is red by design (a suite over zero apps' tests fails); tests/integration/test_gate_scope.py drives it
effect_proof_skip.test-fe-e2e: with a frontend app present, a hermetic clone has no node_modules, which is red by design (a suite over zero apps' tests fails); tests/integration/test_gate_scope.py drives it

evidence._comment: Where make verify writes its evidence record and which schema it follows; read by scripts/gate_evidence.py. dir must be a path .gitignore ignores and no part of it may be a symlink. run_date: the one date a whole gate run calls today (scripts/run_date.py). env names the variable the driver hands every goal, and must be listed in child_env.names; max_age_days is how many days before the clock a date found in that variable may be, which is how long a run may last. Remove run_date and every check reads the clock again.

canary._comment: The release canary, keel's own (scripts/canary.py, make canary): each answer set is rendered fresh and as an update from the last release tag, then fe-install, fe-browsers and make verify run in it (the two frontend targets exit 0 when the project's Makefile FE_APPS names no app). answer_sets maps a set's name to its copier answers over copier.yml's defaults. scratch_root is where the projects render: relative to the checkout and git-ignored, or absolute through KEEL_CANARY_SCRATCH, never under the system temporary directory. step_timeout_minutes kills one step past it; workers is how many projects run at once. A generated project carries the block because its config loader declares the keys; its make canary is a stub.

toolchain._comment: The toolchain versions, one home each; read by scripts/check_toolchain.py. node_major is the Node major every frontend app's lockfile is resolved under: make fe-install refuses another (check_toolchain.py node), and CI's setup-node installs it. python is the release CI's setup-python installs; it must satisfy layers.backend.python and pyproject.toml requires-python (tests/integration/test_toolchain_gate.py), and a generated project takes it from the copier answer toolchain_python, whose validator refuses a release backend_python does not allow. Each workflow job reads both from a step with id toolchain that runs check_toolchain.py versions into $GITHUB_OUTPUT, whose outputs are node and python, never a literal. runner_images is every runs-on label a workflow may use: pinned images only, never a label ending -latest, which moves under the project.

venv._comment: What the venv must hold before a gate runs; read by scripts/check_venv.py, the first prerequisite of make check-all and so the first step of make verify. extras are the pyproject.toml extras the gate imports; the extra each enabled transport names in transports.extras is judged with them. Every requirement of the core dependencies and of those extras, followed through an extra that names the project itself, must be installed at a version its specifier allows, or the check fails before any other goal and names the pip command that installs them.

launcher._comment: Where a long script runs; read by scripts/launch.py, which decides, and scripts/long_scripts.py, which proposes long_scripts entries (docs/adr/keel/K-0020-shared-compute-launcher.md). own_hosts_file is a git-ignored JSON file of fnmatch patterns for the hosts that are one person's own (config/own-hosts.example.json is its shipped twin); absent, unreadable or matching nothing means the host is shared. durations_file is the git-ignored record of each script's last run, keyed by the launch key. A script is long when long_scripts lists it, when its last recorded run took more than long_after_seconds, or when nothing is recorded; long_scripts and default_size give the farm size (cpus, mem_gb, minutes). local_only maps a launch key to the reason it never goes to the farm. credentials maps a launch key to {model_adapter, names}: the only credential names its process may receive. limited.niceness is what running here limited means (os.nice, nothing else). spare.max_load_per_cpu: after the farm did not allocate, this host runs it only when max(load1, load5) / cpus is at most this. farm.adapter names the farm in farm.adapters; the default is none (no farm); an argv adapter submits through its submit argv, with its own bounded wait of wait_seconds, and its reserved not_allocated_status and farm_error_status (1 to 254, not 126, 127 or 130).

evals._comment: Eval harness (evals/, scripts/run_evals.py). threshold: a suite passes when passed/total >= threshold. live.max_calls is the approved spend cap, checked before any call; 0 approves none. live.model null refuses make eval-live.

child_env._comment: The environment a process keel's code starts inherits (docs/adr/keel/K-0012-child-process-environment-allowlist.md). scripts/child_env.py build_child_env starts from an empty dict and copies only these names, a name starting with a prefix, make_targets.unattended_vars and gate_vars (so WRITE_GUARD and the interpreter choice survive a hop through a Python doer), and, for a model adapter, its models.credential_env names; scripts/check_structure.py check_X holds every spawn to it. Why each family: PATH, HOME, USER and LOGNAME to find and run tools; LANG, LANGUAGE, TERM, TZ and LC_ for locale and output; the proxy and CA-bundle names because this network intercepts TLS; GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM so the test suite's hermetic git reaches git, and GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES, because these four choose configuration and the discovery ceiling, not a repository; TEMP, TMP and TMPDIR for scratch; VIRTUAL_ENV and XDG_* for tool caches; SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH for reproducible output; KEEL_REQUIRED_EXTRAS because tests/optional_deps.py reads it to turn a declared surface's skip into a failure, and `make verify` runs its goals through scripts/gate_evidence.py with this environment, so without it a caller who declared a surface required would get a quieter gate than asked for (it carries surface names, never a credential). KEEL_TEST_SCRATCH because tests/conftest.py moves test scratch to the root it names (config tests.scratch_root), so a nested pytest a test starts keeps the root its caller chose. Deliberately absent: every credential (a model adapter's go in models.credential_env), MAKEFLAGS, MFLAGS, MAKELEVEL, MAKEOVERRIDES and MAKEFILES (a nested make must not inherit the outer make's goals; check_X refuses them here), PYTHONPATH (a caller passes it in extra), and GIT_ as a prefix (it would admit GIT_ASKPASS and GIT_SSH_COMMAND). repo_context_names are the variables git binds to the repository it started a process in: `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` (git 2.43.5) plus GIT_NAMESPACE (gitnamespaces(7)) and GIT_QUARANTINE_PATH (githooks(5), pre-receive). githooks(5) tells a hook that runs git in another repository to clear them, so build_child_env drops them unless a call passes repo_context=True, and child_env_policy (hence check_X) refuses names, prefixes, make_targets vars or a models.credential_env list that admits one. config_injection_names and config_injection_prefixes are the configuration-injection family, the variables through which a parent hands git its -c settings (GIT_CONFIG, GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS and the numbered GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n> and GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_<n>, which override GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and reach every hook); they hold no location, so they are not repo context, build_child_env never copies one from the parent, and child_env_policy (hence check_X) refuses names, prefixes, make_targets vars or a models.credential_env list that admits one. credentialed_values maps a variable the allowlist copies to the reason this project's children may receive the credential its value carries (an authenticating proxy's user:password@); build_child_env refuses any other copied value carrying user information (scripts/child_env.py carries_credential: a user part in a URL authority, a whole value user[:password]@host:port, or any user part urllib's proxy parser reads in a *_proxy variable), naming the variable and never the value, and an entry no allowlist source copies is a check_X error. credential_value_patterns maps a label to a regular expression a credential's value matches (an Authorization header, a JWT, an opaque token, a PEM private key); build_child_env and the gate runner search every copied value with each, under the same exemptions, and an error names the variable and the label, never the value or the pattern. login_name_schemes lists the URL schemes whose user part is a login name (ssh://git@host): in one of them a user part counts as a credential only with a password; absent, every user part counts. Empty: no child receives a credential through the allowlist. A credential only one model adapter's child needs belongs in models.credential_env instead. Defence-in-depth, not a sandbox: a same-uid child can still read /proc/$PPID/environ.

journey._comment: The browser journey each frontend app's playwright.config.ts reads (`make test-fe-e2e`): it builds the site, serves it with the stack's own preview server on http://<host>:<port> (an IPv6 host is written without brackets), and waits server_timeout_ms for it before the run fails. A port another process holds fails the run rather than reusing that server. browser_executable null uses the runner's own browser cache, located by PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH when set (child_env.names passes it to every make verify goal); a path launches that browser instead. Nothing here downloads a browser: `make fe-browsers` does, through each app's npm script test:e2e:browsers, and without one in the cache the journey fails.

transports._comment: enabled lists the transports this project serves and available maps each declared transport to its directory (check_H). extras maps an enabled transport to the pyproject.toml extra that installs its packages: scripts/check_venv.py judges that extra installed before make verify runs a goal, and tests/optional_deps.py turns a test's skip over one of its packages into a failure while the transport is enabled.

e2e._comment: End-to-end coverage (CONVENTIONS section 17): every endpoint an enabled transport serves is named by a scenario under scenario_dir with @pytest.mark.<marker>("<transport> <id>"), or exempt here with a reason. tests/integration/test_e2e_coverage.py derives the endpoints from the code, never from a list: sources maps a transport to how (openapi: the app's OpenAPI document, written by openapi_exporter inside the REST transport directory; mcp-stdio: each __main__-guarded server asked over its stdio, with mcp_env added to its environment; proto: the transport's .proto service methods; none: the transport serves no endpoint of its own). list_timeout_s bounds each child a derivation or a scenario starts: the walk over the routes the REST app serves, the exporter, and each MCP server. exempt maps an endpoint id to the reason it has no scenario; a stale, redundant or reasonless entry is red. server is how tests/live_server.py starts the REST app for a scenario: uvicorn serving app on host, ready when probe_path answers 200 within ready_timeout_s (polled every probe_interval_s), each request bounded by request_timeout_s, and stopped by SIGTERM then SIGKILL after stop_timeout_s. There is no port: the OS assigns a free one. make run-api's fixed port is a separate value.

secrets._comment: What keeps a credential out of a file git would commit. tests/integration/test_committed_secrets_gate.py is the keyed layer, keel's own rule with no outside tool: it takes its secret names from scripts/config_loader.py KEYS (each row with secret=True gives its variable name, and its config path when it lives in a file; every models.credential_env name must have one), reads every file a commit could carry (scripts/git_tree.py candidate_files: tracked, staged, and untracked but not ignored; with no repository, every file the structure walk reaches), and judges a file whose basename matches json_files as JSON and one matching dotenv_files as KEY=VALUE lines, its work-tree copy and its index copy both. A value under a secret name is red, naming the file, the line and the key and never the value. The empty value is the only placeholder, because .env.example ships a secret name with nothing after it: in a dotenv file KEY=, KEY="" and KEY='' pass, and changeme or ${OTHER} is a value; in JSON "" and null pass. A file that does not parse as JSON is red, so a commented JSON file needs a basename these patterns do not match. Narrowing either list hides files from the gate: that is a security decision, not a tidy-up. The gate sees a name, not a shape: a credential under a name no secret row declares, in a file type it does not parse, or already in history is not its to see. The scanner is the second layer, for the shapes no name declares: scripts/scan_secrets.py is the gitleaks adapter and runs the program scanner.name names (another name is exit 14, because no adapter writes its flags), which the scanner.hook_repo hook in .pre-commit-config.yaml installs at the release scanner.rev pins (`make secrets-install`, which also writes scanner.record_file with the path, rev and sha256 the history scan runs, so git must ignore that file). Its staged mode judges what a commit would carry, and the commit hook scans every commit instead when nothing is staged; its history mode judges every commit scanner.history_log_opts reaches. A finding prints as file, line and rule, never the value. The scanner is told to exit scanner.leak_exit_code on a finding, so its own crash cannot read as one; a status and report that disagree, and a missing or unrecorded scanner, are exit 11, never a skip, and log options that reach no commit are exit 13. scanner.refused_files are the scanner's own config and ignore file names: a scan refuses to run beside one, because a file under judgement must not decide what is judged. scanner.exclusions excuses one rule in one exact file, each with its reason; an exclusion the history scan does not use is red.

shell._comment: The shell scripts' gates. scripts/shell_gate.py judges every file a commit could carry (scripts/git_tree.py candidate_files) that is a regular file, not a symlink, and either ends in a script_suffixes suffix or opens with a shebang whose interpreter, after `env` and its options, is one of shebang_shells, and that no excluded_paths entry covers (an entry maps a repo-relative path, itself and everything under it, to the reason it is never judged, such as a vendored script; an entry that covers no file a commit could carry is exit 14); a test_suffixes file is a test, which `make test-sh` runs and the lint and format targets do not judge. linter, formatter and test_runner name the tool for each role by its adapter in scripts/shell_gate.py (shellcheck, shfmt and bats today); a name it has no adapter for is exit 14, and a tool on neither the interpreter's directory nor PATH is exit 11 naming the tool, never a skip. Each tool runs under the allowlisted environment (scripts/child_env.py) and its status is the answer. With no shell script and no test file every target is exit 13 unless no_scripts is the reason the project has none, which the target prints before it passes; a no_scripts reason left in place once a shell file exists is exit 14. Shell scripts with no test file, or test files holding no test, are exit 13, because a pass over zero tests proves nothing. enabled is the copier answer `shell`: false makes every shell target say so and run no tool.
shell.no_scripts: keel ships no shell script or shell test: its gates are Python scripts. Set this to null when it adds its first.

tests._comment: Where test scratch lives, and what a test may reach outside itself, by tier. scratch_root is the disk directory test scratch goes under, and memory_scratch_root the memory-backed one a session prefers: tests/conftest.py reads both through scripts/config_loader.py and takes, in order, KEEL_TEST_SCRATCH; memory_scratch_root with -<uid> appended, when its parent exists, its file system has memory_scratch_min_free_mb megabytes free, its parent is not writable by other users without the sticky bit, and the directory is one this user owns with mode 0700 (made so when absent; a link at the configured name is never followed); or scratch_root. Memory comes first because test scratch is thrown away within seconds and needs no durability, and on a network-mounted home every small-file write is a round trip. A host without the parent (macOS has no /dev/shm), a small one (a container's is often 64 MB) or a planted directory falls back to scratch_root, and pytest's header line `scratch:`, which -q hides, names the root in use and why memory was passed over; null turns memory off. It expands ~, and points tempfile, TMPDIR and pytest's numbered basetemp there before any test module is imported; pyproject.toml's tmp_path_retention_policy then removes a passed test's directory and keeps a failed one's, named after the test. It must be absolute, with no .. part, and neither under the system temporary directory, which every program shares and where kept directories pile up unseen, nor inside the checkout, whose tree walkers would read a kept directory; memory_scratch_root is held to the same rule; a refused root, or a memory_scratch_min_free_mb that is negative or absent while memory_scratch_root is set, stops pytest before any test runs. A root that holds the checkout is accepted, and the checkout stays outside it. tests/isolation_guard.py reads this block through scripts/config_loader.py, and tests/conftest.py installs it as a Python audit hook that judges each test's setup, call and teardown. isolation.tiers maps a tier marker to its rule on three axes: network (none: no socket connect, sendto or sendmsg with an address, an AF_UNIX path inside a temp root aside; loopback: also 127.0.0.0/8, ::1 and the name localhost; any: anywhere), writes (temp: a file, directory or link is created, changed or removed, its mode, owner, flags, times or extended attributes changed, or an AF_UNIX socket bound to a path, only under scratch_root or pytest's basetemp; any: anywhere) and stores (temp: a sqlite database is opened only under those roots, a file: name judged both as a URI and as a file in the working directory, and a store listed in isolation.stores is never opened in any mode; any: anywhere). The closest tier marker on a test decides; a test with no marker that names a row here gets the strictest value on every axis. A reach outside the rule fails the test, named, even when the test catches the error. isolation.exempt.<axis> maps a test's node id to the reason it may reach outside its tier on that axis; a blank reason is refused before any test runs, and an exemption whose test ran and reached nothing on that axis fails the run. isolation.stores lists the live stores, relative to the project root or absolute; a test reaches one only through the store_copy fixture, which copies it with its -wal, -shm and -journal siblings into the test's own directory. Defence-in-depth, not a sandbox: a child process is not audited, and a name lookup is not judged, by choice. child_timeout_seconds is how long a test of the shipped harness lets a child Python or a nested pytest session run before it kills it and fails. docs/adr/keel/K-0024-what-a-test-may-reach.md is the decision.

traceability._comment: Requirement traceability (CONVENTIONS section 17): every requirement a `kind: spec` document under specs_root defines is named by a test under tests_root with @pytest.mark.<marker>("<id>"), or excused in gaps with a reason. scripts/trace_requirements.py (make trace) judges it and writes the matrix to matrix_path, whose shape, version and length caps matrix_schema fixes; matrix_path must be git-ignored. id_prefixes is the closed registry of id prefixes: an id is <prefix> then exactly digits ASCII digits, optionally followed by #AC-<n> for one numbered criterion; the longest listed prefix wins and an unlisted prefix is refused. family requirement is what a test covers; family goal is recognised and never traced. source self means a spec here defines the ids; source spine means another system does, so a spec here may not. gaps maps a unit's id (a criterion, or a requirement that has none) to the reason no test names it; a gap for a covered, undefined or malformed id is red. no_requirements is null, or the reason this project has no requirement yet: with zero requirements and null the gate is red, and the reason is red once a requirement or a marker exists.

runtimes._comment: Agent control-flow engines this project makes available (registered in runtimes/registry.py, CONVENTIONS section 16). 'default' is declarative: check_H requires it to be in 'available' and each engine's directory to exist, but runtimes/registry.py DEFAULT_RUNTIME decides what get_runtime() returns with no name, and nothing ties the two together.

models._comment: Model/provider adapters this project makes available (registered in models/registry.py). 'default' is declarative: check_H requires it to be in 'available' and the showcase marks it, but models/registry.py DEFAULT_MODEL decides what get_model() returns with no name, and nothing ties the two together; the showcase surfaces this list. credential_env names, per adapter, the credential environment variables it may use: for an adapter that starts a process, what that process gets on top of child_env (scripts/child_env.py build_child_env(credentials_for=<adapter>)), an adapter absent from it getting the base allowlist only; for openai-compatible, which sends a credential itself, the only names its api_key_env argument accepts. Add a name here, not in code, when a CLI needs one more (for example a cloud provider's region). allowed_hosts names, per adapter that sends a credential itself, the `host` or `host:port` entries it may send it to, each in its one canonical form (scripts/child_env.py canonical_host_entry: a lower-case ASCII name, a dotted-quad IPv4 address or a bracketed compressed IPv6 address); `host` matches only the scheme's default port and nothing matches by suffix, prefix or wildcard. It ships empty, so openai-compatible refuses every base_url, its default included, until the project lists the endpoint's host; an adapter absent from it may send its credential nowhere. Defence in depth, not a sandbox (docs/adr/keel/K-0018-model-endpoint-host-allowlist.md).

import_layers._comment: The layers a Python import may cross, bottom to top: a file may import a file in its own layer or a lower one, never a higher one, so everything flows up. A file sits in the layer of its longest prefix, matched by whole path segments. search_roots are the directories an import name is looked up from, in order, the first holding it winning: the repository root and the sys.path entries keel's entry points and tests add. The order comes from CONVENTIONS section 2 (the directories), src/AGENT.md (app -> {frontend, backend} -> shared) and the measured import graph: scripts/child_env.py and scripts/exit_codes.py, both stdlib-only, sit at the bottom because models, agents, mcp, evals and api import them, and scripts/config_loader.py, stdlib-only too, sits with them as the config reader any layer may import; tests/integration/test_gate_scope.py holds every file of the bottom layer to the oldest interpreter a hook runs, and the rest of scripts/ sits above api, mcp and demo because scripts/doc_review.py imports agents. tests/integration/test_import_layers_gate.py reads search_roots and order and fails an upward import, a file no prefix places, and a prefix on disk that places no file; a prefix whose path is absent, such as a transport this project did not select, is skipped. Place a new top-level directory that holds Python here. may_end_the_process maps a module another non-test module imports to the reason it still ends the process outside its entry block; tests/integration/test_exit_gate.py reads it, and an entry that no longer names such a module, or whose reason is blank, is red. docs/adr/keel/K-0021-imports-flow-up-a-configured-layer-order.md is the decision.

may_end_the_process.scripts/jobs/conflict_guard.py: exit_if_conflicted runs in a job's entry block before the job imports anything else of the project, so there is no main yet to return a member to, and the job's next import may be the conflicted file; it ends the process through exit_codes.fail, imported only at that moment

config_reads._comment: A heuristic over the syntax tree: tests/integration/test_config_reads_gate.py walks the Python files under `roots`, scripts/config_loader.py left out, and fails a direct read of a file scripts/config_loader.py PROJECT_READS declares (an open, read_text or read_bytes of a path built from constants, a bound name, a starred split, another project module's path constant imported by name or read as an attribute, or a same-module helper handed one) and a direct read of a variable the config declares as carrying a value (environ, getenv), because a value read twice is read by two rules; an open for writing counts too. The loader is the one reader, so a default, a type and a secret are judged once. It has known false negatives: a path handed in as a parameter, an attribute of a module imported inside a function or relatively, a function of another module that opens what it is given, a method called through an object, a variable whose name the code holds in a variable, a read through subprocess or importlib, and a path built from a value that is not a constant. tests/ is not walked: it reads config as its own policy and to build fixtures. `allowed` maps each file that still reads directly to the reason; an entry whose reason is blank, whose file is absent or outside the roots, or whose file no longer reads directly is red, and the test's _CEILING caps the count, so the map only shrinks. Where the gate runs tells keel's files from a project's own: in the template repository, which holds copier.yml, every finding is red; in a generated project the two finding tests judge through the expiring tier (`expiring_tier`), so a finding its baseline records warns until `expiring_tier.expires` and any other is red. docs/adr/keel/K-0022-one-config-loader.md is the decision.

allowed.agents/practice_refactor/_brain.py: opens the practices registry under the corpus root its caller hands it, not this project's; it stays until a loader test covers a root an agent is handed
allowed.scripts/audit_project.py: opens the manifest of the generated project it audits, which is data under audit and not this project's configuration
allowed.scripts/check_structure.py: the gate validates the manifest's shape under the oldest host interpreter before any loader row can be trusted, at twelve sites, so moving it onto the loader is a change of its own
allowed.scripts/jobs/declare_no_app.py: rewrites the manifest's text in place, so it reads the file as text to edit, not as configuration
allowed.scripts/jobs/export_showcase_static.py: opens the manifest for layers.frontend inside a copier job; importing the loader would add config/practices.json to the files scripts/jobs/conflict_guard.py refuses the job over, and no test yet proves the job under that refusal
allowed.scripts/jobs/restamp_docs.py: reads the manifest's raw bytes to find a merge-conflict marker before anything parses it, not a configured value
allowed.scripts/launch.py: opens the manifest for the launcher block, whose one reader scripts/long_scripts.py imports; the launcher block has no KEYS rows yet, and the two modules move onto the loader together
allowed.scripts/long_scripts.py: opens the manifest for the launcher block through the reader scripts/launch.py owns, and moves onto the loader with scripts/launch.py
allowed.scripts/run_app.py: opens the manifest for layers.app, where absent and null are two refusals; that split needs a KEYS row and an exit-code decision not yet made
allowed.src/backend/showcase/_repo.py: opens the manifest and the practices registry for the showcase read model, whose keys have no KEYS rows yet
allowed.scripts/trace_requirements.py: opens the manifest for the traceability block, which has no KEYS rows yet
allowed.src/backend/shared/__init__.py: opens the manifest for the project name at import time; through the loader, a read at import would write a default line in every process that imports the package, and whether it should is not decided

expiring_tier._comment: The tier for a generated project's own code (docs/adr/keel/K-0027-a-project-s-own-code-warns-until-a-hard-date.md), read through scripts/config_loader.py by scripts/expiring_tier.py. In the template repository, which holds copier.yml, every finding of a gate test that adopts the tier is red. In a generated project a finding recorded in `baseline` warns until `expires` and is red from that day; a finding with no entry is red at once, and an entry no finding matches is red, so the file only shrinks. `make gate-baseline` (scripts/record_gate_baseline.py) writes `baseline`, and it may add entries only when .copier-answers.yml `_commit` differs from the commit the file records. `expires` is a calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD, no later than scripts/expiring_tier_data.py CEILING, which copier rewrites on every update; an earlier date ends the grace sooner, and a later one is red.

change_comments._comment: A heuristic over the comments that open a thought (tests/source_tree.py comment_starts, read through tokenize, so a string is never a comment): tests/integration/test_change_comment_gate.py fails one whose text, lowercased, starts with a phrase here followed by a character that is not a letter or digit, or by its end, because such a comment reports a change instead of explaining the code (docs/guides/python-style.md section 2). It has known false negatives: a phrase in mid-sentence, and a change reported in other words. A comment opening with one of `directives` is an instruction to a tool (a shebang, a type, lint or coverage pragma, a formatter switch), not prose, and is skipped. Add a phrase when review finds a new opener of that kind.

practices._comment: Domain coding-practice profiles are DEFINED in config/practices.json (ai/cuda/langgraph) and ENABLED here — flip a flag to true to turn its domain checks on (e.g. cuda -> check_L naked-tensor, resource-context-manager advisory). All off keeps the template domain-neutral. Validated by check_structure.py (check_H); consumed by check_L and check_practices.py.
